statement: `min_score grid` returns a result `res`. Call an m-by-n matrix B of positive integers valid if for every row r and columns c1,c2, grid[r][c1] > grid[r][c2] implies B[r][c1] > B[r][c2], and for every column c and rows r1,r2, grid[r1][c] > grid[r2][c] implies B[r1][c] > B[r2][c]. Let K be the least positive integer such that some valid B satisfies B[r][c] <= K for every cell. Then res is valid, so it has shape m-by-n and positive entries, and max over all cells of res equals K.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The slice grid is nonempty, so m >= 1. Let n = len(grid[0]). Every row grid[r] with 0 <= r < m has length n, with 1 <= m <= 1000, 1 <= n <= 1000, and m*n <= 100000. For every r,c with 0 <= r < m and 0 <= c < n, 1 <= grid[r][c] <= 1000000000. All entries of grid are pairwise distinct: for any two distinct cells (r,c) and (r',c'), grid[r][c] != grid[r'][c'].

statement: A same-row-or-column increasing chain is a nonempty finite sequence of cells (r_0,c_0),...,(r_{k-1},c_{k-1}) in the grid such that for each i with 0 <= i < k-1, either r_i = r_{i+1} or c_i = c_{i+1}, and grid[r_i][c_i] < grid[r_{i+1}][c_{i+1}]. Let L be the maximum length k of such a chain. Whenever `min_score grid` returns a result `res`, max over all cells of res equals L.
